payload.claim: A span's `start` and `end` are each independently floored (`math.floor(ceilings.timestamp)`), so two `Ceilings` events that land in the same wall-clock second produce a zero-width half-open interval `[N, N)` that cannot hold any task's `started_at`, not even the task that opened that span. `PREFLIGHT_FAILED` and `RATE_LIMITED` are explicitly not in `scheduler.DONE_STATES`, so a spec can be retried at the same `spec_sha` and the same `events.jsonl` shortly after a fast preflight failure; if the two `Ceilings` timestamps round down to the same second, the earlier task (and anything else legitimately in that span) is wrongly marked `unattributable` and dropped from the projection, silently defeating the N5 guarantee this module exists to check.
